summary.oneLiner: Ashoka Buildcon navigated a transitional FY26 with revenue degrowth (-17% YoY) due to execution delays and conservative accounting (ECL provisions), but successfully monetized 10 assets to strengthen the balance sheet and secured high-value international orders (Saudi Arabia, Angola) that position FY27 for a 20% revenue rebound and margin expansion to double digits.

one-line thesis: Ashoka Buildcon navigated a transitional FY26 with revenue degrowth (-17% YoY) due to execution delays and conservative accounting (ECL provisions), but successfully monetized 10 assets to strengthen the balance sheet and secured high-value international orders (Saudi Arabia, Angola) that position FY27 for a 20% revenue rebound and margin expansion to double digits.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 5,952 Cr (FY26, -17% YoY); Q4 Rev: INR 1,819 Cr (-10% YoY). EBITDA: INR 636 Cr (FY26, -6% YoY); Margin: 10.7% (+130 bps YoY); Q4 Margin: 9.2% (+20 bps YoY) but impacted by INR 28 Cr ECL provision. PAT: INR 320 Cr (FY26); Q4 PAT: INR 49 Cr (-18% YoY). Order Book: INR 15,312 Cr (excl. post-March LOAs); Diversified (Roads 66%, Power T&D 30%). Net Debt: Consolidated INR 2,778 Cr; Standalone Working Capital Debt ~INR 600 Cr (net of cash); Debt to reduce by ~INR 1,300 Cr upon remaining HAM sales.
guidance: Revenue Growth: ~20% for FY27. EBITDA Margin: 9.5%-10.5% (double digit). Order Inflow Target: INR 8,000-10,000 Cr. Capex: ~INR 100 Cr for FY27.
order book & pipeline: Total: INR 15,312 Cr. Breakup: Roads & Railway INR 10,123 Cr (HAM INR 1,619 Cr, EPC Roads INR 7,084 Cr, Railway INR 1,420 Cr); Power T&D INR 4,627 Cr; Buildings INR 562 Cr. Excludes INR 900 Cr (Saudi Hotel) and INR 1,100 Cr (IGR Mumbai) executed at SPV level.
segment / subsidiary detail: Road EPC (50% of Q4 rev), Road HAM (10%), Power T&D (18%), Railway (8%), Others (14%). International wins include Saudi Arabia (INR 900 Cr share), Angola (INR 690 Cr), Liberia (INR 430 Cr). Domestic bridge win in Bihar (INR 242 Cr share).
growth verticals / optionality: Monetization of remaining 6 HAM SPVs (4 by June '26, 2 by Dec '26) releasing ~INR 1,150 Cr cash + deferred consideration. International pipeline expanding in Middle East and Africa. Bid pipeline >INR 1 Lakh Cr (INR 40k Cr NH + INR 30-40k Cr States/others).
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 margins pressured by project prolongation, fixed cost absorption on lower turnover, and INR 28 Cr ECL provision in Q4. Input cost inflation (cement, steel, bitumen) cited as headwind. FY27 guidance assumes 9.5-10.5% margins factoring in potential ECL reversals as payments clear.
capex / expansion: FY26 Capex: INR 67 Cr (Q4: INR 16 Cr). FY27 Guidance: ~INR 100 Cr (includes international project setup).
capital allocation: Priority on debt reduction via asset monetization (10 assets sold in FY26; 6 pending). Expected cash inflow: INR 750 Cr+ by June '26, INR 400 Cr by Dec '26. Deferred consideration of ~INR 550 Cr expected over 24-36 months. Working capital debt target: INR 500-600 Cr by Mar '27.
risks & watch-items: Execution delays due to land acquisition/clearances (ROW). Working capital stretch (debtor days elevated to 5-7 months in Power, 3-3.5 months in Roads). Regulatory uncertainty on NHAI debarment clauses regarding site casualties. Geopolitical risks in international markets.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges FY26 as a 'transition year' with execution challenges but emphasizes strategic consolidation, balance sheet strengthening, and clear visibility on FY27 recovery through monetization and new order flow.
non-obvious takeaways: Significant order book value (INR 2,000 Cr+) resides in SPVs (Saudi/IGR) and does not reflect in standalone ABL order book but will consolidate. ECL provisions are transient; reversals expected as milestone payments clear, artificially suppressing current margins. Deferred monetization proceeds (~INR 550 Cr) tied to NHAI toll extensions create a hidden future cash flow stream.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain constraints and input cost inflation impacting EPC margins across the sector. | UltraTech Cement | beneficiary | Med | Ashoka cites rising cement prices as a key cost pressure; volume recovery in FY27 guidance supports demand. |
| Delayed payments and working capital stretch in power T&D segment. | Power Grid Corp | loser | Low | While not directly named as debtor, Ashoka's comment on 5-7 month billing cycles in power suggests systemic payment delays affecting upstream equipment suppliers too. |
| Need for private capital participation in road infrastructure (BOT model push). | IRB Infrastructure | beneficiary | Med | Govt target of INR 75,000 Cr BOT projects in FY27 benefits established players with monetization track records like Ashoka and peers. |

scorecard.pe_basis: TTM trailing (spec band written for forward P/E)

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
